mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP increases but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment above 4.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rises but employment increases, it indicates a tight labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both unemployment rises and employment increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates negatively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If federal funds rates are high in a tightening cycle but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests economic growth, positively impacting S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: CPI exceeding 3% may lead to rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If CPI exceeds 3% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth with low unemployment indicates a robust economy, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP is strong and unemployment is low but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in housing starts below 1000 signals economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts drop below 1000 but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
